## How GRACE Follow-On Tracks Changes in Earth’s Mass

Launched in 2018, GRACE Follow-On consists of two spacecraft that follow one another about 137 miles (220 kilometers) apart. The mission uses changes in the distance between them—not changes in their altitude—to infer shifts in mass on Earth.

As the pair approaches a larger mass concentration, gravity acts on the leading spacecraft first, initially pulling it farther ahead of the trailing spacecraft and increasing the distance between them. That changing separation is the measurement the mission uses; the spacecraft do not directly image water.

The inferred mass shifts help scientists investigate water movement in groundwater, lakes and rivers, soil, glaciers and ice sheets, as well as sea-level changes associated with water added to the oceans.
